summary: Backend testing of signal derivation and aggregation endpoints. Created /app/backend/tests/test_signals.py with 13 test cases covering derivation (fresh run, invalid_id 400, nonexistent 404), aggregation (batch_id, run_ids CSV, missing params 400, sort order, /pricing top rank), specific signal detection (Arun keyboard_dead_end, Meera dead_click), and sanity endpoints (/api/health, /api/persona-panels). All 13 tests PASS against production URL. Verified: /pricing is top-ranked screen (weighted_score=89.0) in batch ddb4c7d5..., Arun's run has keyboard_dead_end signal, Meera's run has dead_click signal, fresh run derivation returns properly shaped signals (type/severity/source/description). Found one potential minor issue: GET /api/signals list endpoint strips the 'source' and 'count' fields from responses because the Signal Pydantic model (server.py L127-133) doesn't include them — DB has the data, only serialization drops it. Aggregation endpoint (which reads raw DB) works correctly.

minor.issue: Signal Pydantic model (server.py:127) lacks 'source' and 'count' fields, so list_signals/get_signal responses strip these fields from derived signals even though they exist in DB. This makes it impossible for API consumers to filter/inspect signals by source (console_error, keyboard_dead_end, etc.) via the list endpoint. Aggregate endpoint bypasses the model and works fine.

Some /pricing signals show source='unknown' in by_source (3 of 7). Likely engine-emitted signals (e.g., action rejections) that don't set the 'source' field. Consider setting a default source like 'engine' or 'action_rejected' in engine.py to improve aggregation grouping.

action_items: Add 'source: Optional[str] = None' and 'count: Optional[int] = 1' to Signal Pydantic model in /app/backend/server.py (line 127) so list/get endpoints expose these fields.
Consider setting a 'source' field on engine-emitted signals (action rejections, etc.) so they aggregate under a named source rather than 'unknown'.
critical_code_review_comments: Signal model schema drift: signals.py writes 'source' and 'count' to DB but the Signal Pydantic model in server.py doesn't declare them → data invisible via GET /api/signals. Fix by extending the model.

signals.py derive_all_signals inserts without dedup check — repeated POST /api/signals/derive/{run_id} calls will create duplicate rows in DB (as noted in review request itself). Consider deleting existing derived signals or upsert-by-key before inserting.
signals.py _get_signals_for_run cursor.to_list(50) hard-caps steps at 50; if a run has more steps this silently truncates. Consider using cursor.to_list(length=None) or a documented larger limit.
aggregate_signals_by_screen limits signals fetch to 5000 — no pagination and no warning if hit.
